\subsection{Self-Trapped excitons}
Thermal fluctuations induce minor lattice vibrations that act as a trigger, creating a transient local deformation. The strongly localized exciton is captured by this distortion, through massive exciton-phonon coupling, it abruptly discharges its potential energy into the lattice, drastically deepening the local potential well. This intense localized energy weakens and breaks the covalent \(\text{Si\textendash O\textendash Si}\) bond, displacing the oxygen atom from its equilibrium position. This structural rupture generates two dangling bonds, each retaining an unpaired electron. Within this highly distorted configuration, the exciton self-traps: the hole becomes localized on the oxygen dangling bond, while the electron remains bound to the silicon dangling bond.
